slides.title: Efficient Adaptation for Scientific Models

slots.problem: Large models adapt well but make iteration expensive for small research groups @smith2025llm.
slots.method: The paper adds lightweight routing before fine-tuning, then evaluates against strong baselines @nguyen2026routing.
slots.finding: Accuracy improves while inference cost remains stable.

slides.configSource:
authors:
  - A. Smith
  - B. Lee
venue: ICML
year: 2026
keywords:
  - efficient learning
  - adaptation
  - reproducibility

slides.title: Why This Paper Matters
slides.body:
## Motivation

- Prior slide and paper workflows often separate evidence from narrative @lee2024design.
- This paper makes the trade-off explicit: better adaptation without a larger deployment footprint.
- The key question: can routing improve specialization without destabilizing the base representation?

slides.title: Method Pipeline
slides.body: The routing stage is the main intervention; the rest of the pipeline keeps the evaluation controlled.
slides.configSource:
activeStep: 2
steps:
  - title: Curate
    description: Build task-specific data splits
    detail: 12k examples
  - title: Route
    description: Select lightweight adaptation paths
    detail: learned gates
  - title: Validate
    description: Compare with fine-tuning baselines
    detail: 5 random seeds

slides.title: Main Result
slides.body:
- The gain is largest on low-resource task families.
- Reported variance remains narrow across repeated runs.

slots.evidence:
- Benchmark: Scientific Adaptation Suite
- Baseline: full fine-tuning with matched compute

slides.configSource:
heading: Routing improves adaptation without increasing inference cost
label: Accuracy
metric: 94.7
unit: "%"
delta: +3.2 over baseline
baseline: 5-seed average
variant: success

slides.title: Limitations

slots.limitation:
- Requires labeled target-task examples.
- Does not evaluate severe out-of-domain shift.
slots.mitigation:
- Treat the result as evidence for efficient supervised adaptation.
- Use the appendix to separate robustness claims from the main contribution.

slides.configSource:
heading: Boundary Conditions
description: Scope the claim before moving to discussion.

slides.title: Reliable Academic Presentation Systems

slots.problem: Academic talks need dense evidence, but tooling often leaves consistency and verification to manual review @chen2026thesis.
slots.method: This thesis combines semantic theme tokens, workflow templates, and release checks.
slots.finding: The resulting system reduces authoring drift while preserving Slidev flexibility.

slides.configSource:
authors:
  - Your Name
venue: Thesis Defense
year: 2026
keywords:
  - reliability
  - academic tooling
  - evaluation

slides.title: Evaluation Plan
slides.body: The evaluation pairs mechanical checks with workflow-level review @smith2025llm.
slides.configSource:
cols: 2
experiments:
  - name: Visual QA
    setup: Theme matrix across modes
    result: 72
    metric: screenshots
    note: Covers quote, code, table, and highlight states
  - name: Citation QA
    setup: Doctor and VS Code diagnostics
    result: 5
    metric: issue classes
    note: Catches missing setup and unresolved keys
  - name: Template QA
    setup: Initialize every curated workflow
    result: 5
    metric: templates
    note: Validates package replacement and references
  - name: User Fit
    setup: Paper talk and defense dry runs
    result: qualitative
    metric: feedback
    note: Focuses on presenter friction

slides.title: Limitations

slots.limitation:
- The system focuses on academic Slidev decks, not general web design.
- The templates encode common workflows but cannot replace domain-specific judgment.
slots.mitigation:
- Keep APIs narrow and documented.
- Use the appendix to separate implementation details from the main argument.

slides.configSource:
heading: Boundary Conditions
description: State what the thesis does not claim.

slides.title: Defense Question
slides.body: The checks were derived from observed failures in color contrast, citation setup, and stale authoring metadata.

slots.evidence:
- Semantic token checks prevent dark highlight backgrounds from inheriting dark text.
- Citation diagnostics catch missing bibliography files before presenting.
- Curated templates are initialized and checked as real projects.
slots.followup: The next evaluation should include external users building one deck from scratch.
